title: Mobile Phone Free Classroom
synopsis: Some universities in China are implementing the “phone free classroom” to deal with students who play with their phone instead of paying attention to class. Does it work?

fullText.simplified:
无手机课堂

    你在听课的时候会玩手机吗？
    拿手机看新闻、玩游戏……这已经成为了大学生每天的生活习惯，这样的习惯被很多大学生带到了课堂。于是，课堂上出现了这样的一群人—课堂“低头族”。
    为了让课堂“低头族”能抬起头来认真听课，最近，很多大学都在推行“无手机课堂”。那么，没有手机的课堂，是不是真的能让“低头族”抬起头来认真听课呢？
    孙月是一名大一的学生，她说自己以前的“手机依赖症”很严重，上课时，总会低头看手机，要么玩微信，要么看小说。有时上课忘了带手机，就会感到很无聊。现在她参加了“无手机课堂”，玩手机的时间少了，感觉听课的效率提高了，生活比以前更轻松了。
    但是也有很多人和孙月的想法不同，他们觉得交手机不能保证学生认真听课，学生是不是认真听课，是由老师的上课水平决定的。交手机确实能让“低头族”不那么依赖手机，但是如果老师上课很无聊，有些同学就会很想睡觉，以前有手机的时候还可以玩玩手机，提提神，现在没有手机了，就只能睡觉了，而且一睡就是一节课。
    笔者觉得“无手机课堂”确实能为学生创造一个比较好的听课环境，但是更重要的还是应该教导学生，让学生养成良好的使用手机的习惯。
fullText.traditional:
無手機課堂

    你在聽課的時候會玩手機嗎？
    拿手機看新聞、玩遊戲……這已經成為了大學生每天的生活習慣，這樣的習慣被很多大學生帶到了課堂。於是，課堂上出現了這樣的一群人—課堂“低頭族”。
    為了讓課堂“低頭族”能抬起頭來認真聽課，最近，很多大學都在推行“無手機課堂”。那麼，沒有手機的課堂，是不是真的能讓“低頭族”抬起頭來認真聽課呢？
    孫月是一名大一的學生，她說自己以前的“手機依賴症”很嚴重，上課時，總會低頭看手機，要麼玩微信，要麼看小說。有時上課忘了帶手機，就會感到很無聊。現在她參加了“無手機課堂”，玩手機的時間少了，感覺聽課的效率提高了，生活比以前更輕鬆了。
    但是也有很多人和孫月的想法不同，他們覺得交手機不能保證學生認真聽課，學生是不是認真聽課，是由老師的上課水平決定的。交手機確實能讓“低頭族”不那麼依賴手機，但是如果老師上課很無聊，有些同學就會很想睡覺，以前有手機的時候還可以玩玩手機，提提神，現在沒有手機了，就只能睡覺了，而且一睡就是一節課。
    筆者覺得“無手機課堂”確實能為學生創造一個比較好的聽課環境，但是更重要的還是應該教導學生，讓學生養成良好的使用手機的習慣。

raw.synopsis: Some universities in China are implementing the “phone free classroom” to deal with students who play with their phone instead of paying attention to class. Does it work?
sentence_translations: Mobile phone free classroom
Do you play with your mobile phone during class?
Grabbing the mobile phone to read news and play games...
This has already become a daily habit for university students, and a lot of students bring this habit with them into the classroom.
As a result of this, a certain group has appeared in the classroom – the classroom “head bowing group”.
To make the “head bowing group” lift their heads and pay attention to class, recently a lot of universities implement the “mobile phone free classroom”.
So, without mobile phones in the classroom, does the “head bowing group” really lift up their heads and pay attention to class?
Sun Yue is a first year university student, and she says that she was previously gravely addicted to her mobile phone.
During class, she would always bow down her head to look at her phone, to check WeChat or read novels.
Sometimes she would forget to bring her phone to class, and would get extremely bored.
Now she has joined the “mobile phone free class room” and the time she spends playing with her phone has decreased.
She feels that her productivity in class has increased and that her lifestyle is simpler than before.
A lot of people do not agree with Sun Yue however.
They believe handing over your phone does not guarantee that students will pay attention to class.
Whether students pay attention in class or not is decided by the teacher's level of teaching.
Handing over your phone can make the “head bowing group” less dependent on their phones, ..
.. but if the teaching is not interesting, some students will get sleepy.
Before when they had phones, they could play with their phone for a bit to freshen up their mind.
Now without phones they have no choice but to take a nap, and once they fall asleep they will miss the entire class.
The author feels that the “mobile phone free classroom” can create a better learning environment for students, ..
.. but more importantly you must guide students into creating healthy habits for using their phones.
